---
title: "check-double-inequalities.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a double inequality in math.
psw's rule
["Avoiding double inequalities"](https://morrison-lab.github.io/psw/notation.html#avoiding-double-inequalities)
prefers interval membership, which says the constraint once:
`x \in (a, b)` rather than `a < x < b`,
and `p \in [0, 1]` rather than `0 \le p \le 1`.

The check reads `$...$` and `$$...$$` math
on lines a pull request adds,
in `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.md` files.
It flags a clause made of exactly three operands
joined by two order relations that point the same way:
`<`, `\lt`, `\le`, `\leq`, `\leqslant`, `\prec`, `\preceq`,
their Unicode forms, or their `>` mirrors.
Each finding reports the file, the line, and the clause as written.

## Clauses and groups

A clause ends at a separator
(`,`, `;`, `:`, `&`, `\\`, `\quad`, a text command such as `\text{...}`,
or a quantifier)
and at a logical connective (`\land`, `\lor`, `\implies`, ...),
using the tokenizer and parser of
[check-precedence-parens](check-precedence-parens.qmd).
A group is checked on its own:
parentheses, brackets, braces, and a macro argument,
so the event in `\Pr{a < X \le b}` is a clause too.

The check does not flag:

- a chain of three or more relations (`x_1 < x_2 < \dots < x_n`),
  or one mixing in `=` (`a \le b = c`),
  which is an ordering or a derivation
  rather than a constraint on one quantity;
- relations that point opposite ways (`a < x > b`);
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following,
  `<!-- check-double-inequalities: allow: <reason> -->`.
  The reason is required, so a bare `allow` does not exempt the line.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block,
and a page converts when someone edits it.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the double inequalities a repository still carries.
Measured 2026-11-24 with `whole-tree: true`:
66 hits in Morrison-Lab/pds and 6 in Morrison-Lab/psw,
the psw ones all on the pages that state the rule.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Limitations

- Each line is read on its own,
  so a clause split across lines is checked in pieces.
- A two-step bound in a derivation,
  such as `\E{X} \le A \le B`, is flagged.
  Write it as two relations on separate lines, or allow it with a reason.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when a double inequality is found. Set `false` to warn only. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-double-inequalities.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a double inequality in math on lines a PR adds,
# such as `a < x < b` or `0 \le p \le 1`, where interval membership
# (`x \in (a, b)`, `p \in [0, 1]`) says it once.
# Blocks by default; existing pages never block, since only added lines count.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check math for double inequalities

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-double-inequalities.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'mds/**,notes/**'         # skip submodules and known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-double-inequalities.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-double-inequalities.yml)
for the full caller stub.
